records.gloss: For the director, a psalm of David, a song.
pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David. A song.

L.1: For the director. A psalm of David. A song.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David, for singing.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.
As in 4:1.
The first word (mizmor) is a song sung to music, the second (shir) the general word for a song; Psalms 65-68 all carry both.

The psalm praises God who hears prayer and forgives (verses 2-5), rules nature and the nations (6-9), and sends rain and harvest (10-14). It may have been sung at a harvest festival, when vows were paid (verse 2).
Readable keeps the two words without naming two kinds of song.

records.heading: Praise for the God who sends rain

records.source: לְךָ֤ דֻֽמִיָּ֬ה תְהִלָּ֓ה אֱלֹ֘הִ֥ים בְּצִיּ֑וֹן וּ֝לְךָ֗ יְשֻׁלַּם־נֶֽדֶר׃
records.gloss: To you silence [is] praise, God, in Zion, and to you will be paid a vow.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, in Zion, silence is praise, \q and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} vows will be kept.

L.2: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silence [is] praise, God, in Zion, \q and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a vow will be paid.

R.2: God, in Zion we praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, even in quiet waiting. \q We will keep the promises we made to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: silence is praise: quiet trust as worship
alternatives: praise is fitting for you (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (dumiyyah) means silence or stillness, as in 62:2. The ancient Greek translation read it from a similar word meaning "it is fitting": "praise is fitting for you". Others take it as "praise waits for you".

decisions.choice: a vow paid: a promise kept with an offering
decisions.reason: As in 61:9, people paid vows at the sanctuary when God had answered their prayers (Leviticus 7:16).
Readable names the worshipers.

records.gloss: [You who] hear prayer, to you all flesh will come.
pieces: You hear prayer; \q all people will come before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.3: [You who] hear prayer, \q to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all flesh will come.

R.3: You listen to prayer, \q so everyone will come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness (56:5; 145:21).
Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means (m1).

records.source: דִּבְרֵ֣י עֲ֭וֺנֹת גָּ֣בְרוּ מֶ֑נִּי פְּ֝שָׁעֵ֗ינוּ אַתָּ֥ה תְכַפְּרֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Matters of iniquities are too strong for me; our transgressions — you atone for them.
pieces: Wrongdoings overwhelm me, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cover over our rebellions.

L.4: Matters of iniquities are too strong for me; \q our transgressions — {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} atone for them.

R.4: My sins are too much for me, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgive our wrongs.

decisions.reason: The verb (kipper) means to cover or wipe clean; when God does it, he takes away the guilt of sin (78:38; 79:9).
The speaker feels his own sins and then speaks for the whole people.
Balanced and Readable add "but" to show the turn from sin to forgiveness.

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֤י׀תִּֽבְחַ֣ר וּתְקָרֵב֮ יִשְׁכֹּ֪ן חֲצֵ֫רֶ֥יךָ נִ֭שְׂבְּעָה בְּט֣וּב בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ קְ֝דֹ֗שׁ הֵיכָלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is the one whom] you choose and bring near; he will dwell [in] your courts. May we be satisfied with [the] goodness of your house, [the] holy [place] of your temple.
pieces: How blessed are those whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} choose and draw close, to dwell in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts! \q May we feast on the goodness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy temple.

L.5: How blessed [is the one whom] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} choose and bring near; {{gender:they|he}} will dwell [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts. \q May we be satisfied with the goodness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house, \q the holy [place] of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple.

R.5: Life is truly good for the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} choose and bring close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, to live in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple courts. \q May the good things in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy house fill us with joy.

decisions.choice: how blessed: how happy and favored
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, the word ('ashre) describes the good life of those whom God favors.

decisions.choice: bring near, courts: access to the sanctuary
decisions.reason: To be brought near is to be allowed to come before God in his courts, like the priests (Numbers 16:5) and the worshipers (84:3, 11).

decisions.choice: the goodness of your house: the blessings found there
alternatives: the good things of your house (the feasts of the sacrifices)
decisions.reason: The goodness may include the meals eaten at the sanctuary when offerings were made (36:9).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says what "blessed" means here.
The Hebrew speaks of one person who stands for all whom God chooses; Balanced and Readable make it plural.

records.source: נ֤וֹרָא֨וֹת׀בְּצֶ֣דֶק תַּ֭עֲנֵנוּ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֑נוּ מִבְטָ֥ח כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אֶ֝֗רֶץ וְיָ֣ם רְחֹקִֽים׃
records.gloss: Awesome [things] in righteousness you answer us, God of our salvation, [the] trust of all [the] ends of [the] earth and [the] sea far away,
pieces: With deeds that inspire awe {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer us in righteousness, God of our rescue, \q trusted by all the ends of the earth \q and by those on the far-off seas,

L.6: [With] awesome things in righteousness {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer us, God of our salvation, \q the trust of all the ends of the earth \q and of the far-off sea,

R.6: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save us. You answer us by doing amazing things that are right and fair. \q People everywhere on earth trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q even those who live far across the sea.

decisions.choice: awesome things: deeds that make people fear and wonder
decisions.reason: The word (nora'ot) is used of God's great acts, as at the Exodus (106:22).

decisions.choice: the trust of all the ends of the earth
decisions.reason: God is the one in whom even distant peoples can put their hope; the psalm looks beyond Israel (verse 3).
The sentence continues into verse 7, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.gloss: [who] establishes mountains by his strength, girded with might,
pieces: who fixed the mountains in place by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \q wearing might like a belt,

L.7: who establishes [the] mountains by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength, \q girded with might,

R.7: By {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power God set the mountains firmly in place. \q He is dressed in strength.

decisions.choice: his: a turn to speaking of God
decisions.reason: The praise moves from "you" to "he", as hymns often do.

decisions.choice: girded with might: strength worn like a belt
decisions.reason: A belt was put on for work or battle (93:1; 18:33).
The sentence continues into verse 8, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
Readable starts a new sentence and names God.

records.source: מַשְׁבִּ֤יחַ׀שְׁא֣וֹן יַ֭מִּים שְׁא֥וֹן גַּלֵּיהֶ֗ם וַהֲמ֥וֹן לְאֻמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: [who] stills [the] roar of seas, [the] roar of their waves, and [the] tumult of peoples.
pieces: who quiets the thunder of the seas and the crash of their waves, \q and the uproar of the nations.

L.8: who stills the roar of [the] seas, the roar of their waves, \q and the tumult of [the] peoples.

R.8: He calms the roaring seas and their crashing waves. \q He also calms the noisy, angry nations.

decisions.reason: The raging sea stands for all that threatens God's order, and the raging nations are like it (46:3-7; 89:10).

records.source: וַיִּ֤ירְא֨וּ׀יֹשְׁבֵ֣י קְ֭צָוֺת מֵאוֹתֹתֶ֑יךָ מ֤וֹצָֽאֵי־בֹ֖קֶר וָעֶ֣רֶב תַּרְנִֽין׃
records.gloss: And they fear, [the] dwellers of [the] ends, from your signs; [the] goings-out of morning and evening you make shout for joy.
pieces: Those who live at the far edges of the world stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make the lands of sunrise and sunset sing for joy.

L.9: And the dwellers at the ends [of the earth] fear because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} signs; \q the goings-out of morning and evening {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make shout for joy.

R.9: People who live far away are amazed at the wonderful things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do. \q From where the sun rises to where it sets, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make people shout for joy.

decisions.choice: the goings-out of morning and evening: east and west
alternatives: the times of morning and evening
decisions.reason: The places where the morning comes out and the evening goes are the east and the west, the whole world.
The signs are the deeds that show God's power, in nature and in history.

records.source: פָּקַ֥דְתָּ הָאָ֨רֶץ׀וַתְּשֹׁ֪קְקֶ֡הָ רַבַּ֬ת תַּעְשְׁרֶ֗נָּה פֶּ֣לֶג אֱ֭לֹהִים מָ֣לֵא מָ֑יִם תָּכִ֥ין דְּ֝גָנָ֗ם כִּי־כֵ֥ן תְּכִינֶֽהָ׃
records.gloss: You have visited the earth and made it overflow; greatly you enrich it; [the] stream of God [is] full of water; you prepare their grain, for so you prepare it.
pieces: You pay a visit to the earth and soak it with rain; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make it richly fertile. \q God's channel is brimming with water; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} supply people with grain, \q for this is how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared the land.

L.10: You have visited the earth and made it overflow; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} greatly enrich it; \q the stream of God [is] full of water; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} provide their grain, \q for so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} prepare it.

R.10: You take care of the earth and send rain on it. You make the soil rich. \q God's rivers in the sky are full of water. \q You give people grain to eat, because that is how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made the land.

decisions.reason: The verb (paqad) is used of God coming to see to someone's needs (8:5).

decisions.choice: the stream of God: the source of rain
decisions.reason: The "stream of God" is the water God stores above the sky and sends as rain (Job 38:25), in a land that depends on rain for its harvest.

decisions.choice: their grain ... prepare it: people's grain, the land prepared
decisions.reason: "Their" is the people of the land; "it" is the land, which God has made ready for growing grain.
Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: תְּלָמֶ֣יהָ רַ֭וֵּה נַחֵ֣ת גְּדוּדֶ֑יהָ בִּרְבִיבִ֥ים תְּ֝מֹגְגֶ֗נָּה צִמְחָ֥הּ תְּבָרֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Its furrows watering abundantly, pressing down its ridges, with showers you soften it; its growth you bless.
pieces: Pouring water into its furrows and pressing down its ridges, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make the soil soft with rain showers \q and bless all that springs up from it.

L.11: Watering its furrows abundantly, settling its ridges, \q with showers {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} soften it; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bless its growth.

R.11: You pour rain on the plowed fields and smooth out the lumps of soil. \q You make the ground soft with rain, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bless the plants as they grow.

decisions.choice: furrows and ridges: the plowed field
decisions.reason: The autumn rains softened the ground after plowing; the clods between the furrows are settled and broken down.

records.source: עִ֭טַּרְתָּ שְׁנַ֣ת טוֹבָתֶ֑ךָ וּ֝מַעְגָּלֶ֗יךָ יִרְעֲפ֥וּן דָּֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: You have crowned [the] year of your goodness, and your tracks drip [with] fatness.
pieces: You set a crown on the year of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness, \q and the tracks of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariot drip with richness.

L.12: You have crowned the year of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tracks drip [with] fatness.

R.12: You give a whole year of good things, like a crown. \q Everywhere {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} leave rich food behind.

decisions.choice: crowned the year: given the year its glory
decisions.reason: The harvest is the crown of the year, God's gift at its end.

decisions.choice: your tracks: the paths of your chariot
decisions.reason: The word (ma'gal) is a cart track. God is pictured driving over the land in his storm chariot, and where his wheels go, rain and plenty follow (18:11; 68:5).
As in 63:6, fat stands for the best and richest.
Balanced names what makes the tracks (m2).

records.source: יִ֭רְעֲפוּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר וְ֝גִ֗יל גְּבָע֥וֹת תַּחְגֹּֽרְנָה׃
records.gloss: They drip, [the] pastures of [the] wilderness, and [with] joy [the] hills gird themselves.
pieces: Even the pastures of the open country drip with plenty, \q and the hills put on joy like a belt.

L.13: The pastures of [the] wilderness drip, \q and the hills gird themselves [with] joy.

R.13: Even the grass in the dry country is wet with rain. \q The hills seem to be dressed in joy.

decisions.reason: The word (midbar) is open country with little rain, used for grazing, not only barren desert.

decisions.choice: the hills gird themselves with joy
decisions.reason: The hills, green with growth, are pictured as wearing joy like a belt (compare verse 7).

records.source: לָבְשׁ֬וּ כָרִ֨ים׀הַצֹּ֗אן וַעֲמָקִ֥ים יַֽעַטְפוּ־בָ֑ר יִ֝תְרוֹעֲע֗וּ אַף־יָשִֽׁירוּ׃
records.gloss: They are clothed, the pastures, [with] the flocks, and valleys cover themselves [with] grain; they shout for joy; also they sing.
pieces: Flocks cover the pastures like clothing, \q and grain wraps the valleys; \q they cry out in triumph, yes, they sing!

L.14: The pastures are clothed [with] the flocks, \q and [the] valleys wrap themselves [with] grain; \q they shout for joy; yes, they sing.

R.14: Sheep fill the fields like a coat. \q The valleys are covered with grain. \q Everything shouts and sings for joy!

decisions.reason: The word (kar) can mean a pasture or a young ram; here the pastures are clothed with flocks.

decisions.choice: they shout, they sing: all creation praises
decisions.reason: The fields themselves seem to sing for joy at the harvest (96:12; 98:8).
